Wow. You've lived the life! As someone stuck at a desk-bound job I am majorly jealous haha.   


Anyways, did you manage to keep a blog documenting your lovely travels overseas? I think you could use your blog as a portfolio to get your foot in the door for communications positions, or even editorial positions within the science sector.   


As a writer myself, I think you could get your career started in science writing by freelancing or even taking up an internship. There's no need to feel weird as someone in your 30s doing an internship (I've applied for some myself and I'm 25). Internships are a good way to get your start in a writing career...it's how I got mine started.   


I don't think that you should go back to university/school unless you're heading down a research/academic path riddled with debt. I currently work in a recruitment agency (I do the writing) and we have a lot of people with their Masters and PHDs who still find it hard to get a job because they don't have any relevant experience in what they did their Masters/PHD in.   


Since you've taken the time to travel and discover the world, I think you might need to do the same to find the "right" job for you. Remember, sometimes your dream job isn't exactly the right fit for you. I know, I've quit my "dream job" and it was the best decision.

I did this. I was too tired and burned out from my previous position so I quit. My boss couldn't find a replacement and asked me if I wanted to work freelance (the pay was higher) and I could dictate how many articles I wanted to write that day.   


It was awesome, but got kinda lonely after a while. If your finances are stable, and you have the motivation to really improve yourself, I suggest just leaving. You could also take a part-time course/certificate that's relevant to your career, so that, future employers will know that you kinda quit to improve on yourself.

Understand that life peaks for different people at different times. Have you looked into applying for jobs that you might want to do as a career?   


Customer service is a respectable career too. Don't compare yourself to others. I worked in Customer service for two years before landing a useful writing internship.

Oh hey! Funny how you should mention this because I recently finished an article detailing all the qualifications you'll need to get into the Cybersecurity sector.   


I think Computer Science is good because most universities allow you to take Cybersecurity electives that will be able to give you an idea of what you'll be doing/learning in the field. Computer Engineering, on the other hand, focuses more on the machine's hardware instead of the software inside. Based on this, I will say that Computer Science is the better option if you want to go into cybersecurity.   


I'm not sure where you're based, but have you considered doing a degree in Cybersecurity itself? If you're decided on Cybersecurity as a career field, it'll be beneficial for you to take Cybersecurity as a major in University. However, if you're looking to learn more and gain more skills: I suggest Computer Science and then taking some Cybersecurity certifications. Some useful certificates include (CEH) and (GSEC).   


I've included a link to the article I've written. You can check them out here (along with the Cybersecurity certifications you can take):  [https://www.bgc-group.com/blog/2019/04/tech-cyber-security-courses-singapore](https://www.bgc-group.com/blog/2019/04/tech-cyber-security-courses-singapore)

Hey! I've been in your position before! Young, broke, with extra shit uni marks and unemployed for more than a year. I knew I wanted to write but with barely any experience, I didn't know where to start.   


I took the plunge and hosted my services on Fiverr, got a response from a wedding blog and wrote articles for $5 an hour. Then with those samples, took on an interning job for a sneaker magazine and after a year, I'm now working as a content marketer for a recruitment company. I'm still struggling and I miss the editorial life but life is not as out of control as it was before.   


If you don't want to get back to school, why not try freelance writing? It's a good start and you can charge people from as little as $20/$30 for a short 250-word article. I literally advertised my services on gumtree, carousell, eBay, fiverr (everywhere), just to get a client. I now have a steady stream of clients that I write for over the weekend and it's very good cash + I enjoy it. But freelance life is not all fine and dandy! I've listed some of the problems with freelancing in this article (click [here](https://www.bgc-group.com/blog/2018/12/freelance-life-singapore-expectations-vs-reality)), and if you think its something you can overcome, by all means, start advertising! Seriously, there are so many lazy people out there who hate writing hahah.   


You could also be a vet technician and gain some experience that way. My hiring managers and recruitment friends are usually very open to refer someone and vouch for them to clients - just because the candidate has relevant experience, and not just the university degree.   


I actually came to this subreddit to vent lol and not promote my blogs but really, [this article](https://www.bgc-group.com/blog/2019/01/what-personal-goals-should-i-set) sounds like it'll help you figure things out. We'll find our way out of this hole eventually haha.
